title: MZ Trying to make MGS Peace Walker style base/unit management system

posts.author: Beagleby
posts.body:
Hello! First time poster. As the title says, I'm trying to create a mini game that is heavily inspired by the base building section of MGS Peacewalker. For context I run a D&D game and I wanted this to be a little thing the players could boot up each session and do together for fun, but as such I've remapped most of the base actor/class stats to
kiiind of
work along the lines of 5e D&D with ability scores and such (it's a work in progress).
In terms of plugins I currently have the Visustella CoreEngine and all their Tier 1 Core plug ins (since the Core Engine seems to be designed to work best with all the rest??) mostly just to let me mess around with all the parameters at the moment. I don't think I've used any of the plug in functionality for the actual 'programming'.
Worth saying that I'm pretty new to RPG Maker and I'm definitely not a coder, though I do understand the logic of loops, if statements, etc. and I've watched a lot of tutorials and I'm starting to slowly get my head around it.
Essentially I'm trying to set it up so the player can recruit goblins and assign them to one of 4 or 5 departments within the base. Each goblin is currently an Actor with 6 base parameters/stats and each department would have a score based on two of those stats. I have a doc on how I think the different departments should generate their overall scores and how those scores interact to, etc. but currently I'm stuck on how to set up how the player would interact at all with these systems.
I've managed to set up a little event where a random number of completely blank actors (1-3) are added to the party, given a random profile picture from a selection of 4, randomly assigned a set of stats (from a set pool of values to be based on player level), and then the player can name each one. So recruitment is sorted, but I'm stuck on how to set up the menus to assign to departments and keep track of which goblin is where.
In terms of assigning each goblin to a different department I've had a few ideas: the one that made the most sense to my tiny novice mind was to have a State for each department that gets assigned via an NPC, then use that to search the party for which goblins are in which department and access their scores to calculate the department score. If that makes sense... I have read that you can store arrays as a single variable, which seems promising, but I can't for the life of me get it working for searching the party. I'm also completely bamboozled for how to set up a UI to interact with these systems, I kind of thought there would be some functionality within RPG Maker for doing something like making/customising menus but I've been struggling to even find a plugin that does exactly the sort of thing I'm looking for.
Any advice for plugins, tutorials,  just general directions to look in all very much appreciated! Even if your advice is "RPG maker is not the software to make this in" that would probably be useful haha.. And apologies for the very long post, it's hard to know how much detail is too much.

posts.author: rpgLord69
posts.body:
Not sure what you're doing, but if you want to assign dudes to the base, I think you can just have some event on the center of the map that has choices like:
-assign room 1 member
-assign room 2 member
-assign room 3 member
Then when you select the room you get a choice which actor (party index) to attach:
-actor 1 (index 0)
-actor 2 (index 1)
-actor 3 (index 2)
Store that index to a variable in the show choices.
Then when you've selected the actor, each room checks different stats. If your room checks attack and luck and counts them together, you can script it with like:
const index  = $gameVariables.value(id) // select variable id where you stored the index)
const atk = $gameParty.members()[index].atk;
const luk = $gameParty.members()[index].luk;
$gameVariables.setValue(id, atk+luk); // select another variable id to store the room value
Then you can have events in the rooms that change based on your selections to show the dude you put there.
Oh and you also need to write the system so that if you try to put a dude in a room that is already in a room, it "nulls" the data of the previous room when it switches the dude to the new place.
